newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler says expects higher 1997 operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says expects higher 1997 operating profit.

text.p: German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG, reported a 12 percent increase in first quarter sales to 25.9 billion marks on Wednesday and said it expected another increase in operating profit for 1997.

Daimler said "the good order situation" in the first quarter led it to expect "the pleasing business development to continue in the coming months as well", in particular due to the stronger dollar against the mark.

"On this basis, and as a consequence of the present strength of the U.S. dollar, we expect the operating profit to increase yet again this year," Daimler said in a report issued at its annual news conference.

Daimler, which follows U.S. GAAP accounting rules, saw its operating profit rise to 2.42 billion marks in 1996 compared with an operating loss of 7.198 billion marks in 1995 due to a 5.7 billion mark loss as part of a major restructuring plan.
Daimler said it predicted economic growth to be "only moderate at best" for 1997 and that growth in passenger car and commercial vehicle markets will be limited in the next months.
But Daimler said it expected its automotive business "to develop significantly more favourably than the industry on the whole in 1997".

Daimler also said it expected revenues from its Dasa aerospace business division to grow "markedly" in 1997, above all due to what it called "pleasing developments" for orders in the civil aircraft sector.
The Stuttgart-based group also said it expected the service industry to be one of the world's most dynamic growth sectors in 1997 and for its Debis unit to benefit.
"The services division will take advantage of the opportunities connected with this growth and expects to be able to sustain the positive development of recent years," Daimler said in the report.

In addition, Daimler said it expected a steady increase in business in its directly managed business units, which include its 50 percent stake in railroad equipment supplier Adtranz, engine maker MTU and a microelectronics business.
